topics.topic: Ownership, definitions, and exports of models M13–M28
questions: Which module owns M13–M28 as models, including their definitions and changes: `models`, the modules that embed their values, or `data_provider` for M22–M28?
Which module owns the definitions and type validity of M13–M28 now that State 1 declares them but `models` owns only M01–M12?
Which module owns and exports M13–M28, now that `data_provider` and other modules directly name those models but `models` owns only M01–M12?

quotes:
Reopened on 2026-11-25: the assembled specification held sixteen runtime
models with no record here (the identity closure's `missing_state1_model`).
None adds a concept: each is a value a model above already names, or a row of
a table of the release, and each now has its record — the two forms of a
pointer's publisher (M13, M14), the five forms of an audit entry's subject
(M15–M19), the owner session's pending confirmation and uploaded file (M20,
M21; the upload number, which State 6 carried on the owner's word of
2026-11-24, is now a fact of M11), and the rows of the data provider's seven
tables (M22–M28).

The models M01–M12 as the domain's vocabulary, the declared vocabularies of
State 1 as enumerations — for the artifact types only the shape of a type
with its owner service, whose rows are `data_provider`'s, so a stored
pointer of a type a later release removed still reads (A22 rule 4) — and the disclosure class
of every fact ("Disclosure classes by field"),
the order of the classes (A09 rule 4), and the refusal vocabulary: each refusal
kind with the stage of A04 rule 6 it belongs to.

`models`, for exactly the row models and enumerations of its seven tables:
`ArtifactTypeOwner` (a type with its owner service) and `ServiceName` for
`ARTIFACT_TYPE_OWNERS`; `ServiceRight` (a service and an operation) with
`ServiceName` and `ServiceOperation` for `SERVICE_RIGHTS`;
`ServiceHighestClass` (a service and its highest class) with `ServiceName`
and `DisclosureClass` for `SERVICE_HIGHEST_CLASSES`; `PersonalDataField` (an
answer model's name and a field's) for `PERSONAL_DATA_FIELDS`;
`RefusalHttpStatus` (a code and its status) with `RefusalCode` for
`REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES`; `OwnerActionRoute` (an owner action, its method and
path, whether it is a change and whether it touches an uploaded file) with
`OwnerAction` for `OWNER_ACTIONS`; `OwnerAuditAction` (an owner action,
a customer mark's transition or a project erasure's kind where the action
has one, and the audit action it writes) with `OwnerAction`,
`CustomerTransition`, `ProjectErasure` and `AuditAction` for
`OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`. Its other constants are scalars and import nothing.
judgement.divergence: One implementer extends `models` to own and export M13–M28, so consumers import the declared types; another applies the M01–M12 boundary literally and either relocates the later models or leaves their imports unresolved, which the generator and developer observe.
judgement.why: State 1 declares M13–M28 and State 3 requires consumers to know several of them through `models`, but State 3 assigns `models` ownership only through M12 and assigns no alternative owner for the later model definitions.

witness.initial: The specification contains State 1 models M13–M28, and generation reaches a `data_provider` that directly names the M22–M28 row models.
events: The specification generator follows the `models` ownership statement when constructing that module's exported model vocabulary.
The generator constructs `data_provider`, whose declared dependency on `models` names the M22–M28 row types.
outcomes: The implementer treats all State 1 models as `models` exports, so the imports resolve and generation continues.
The implementer treats the M01–M12 limit literally, so the named row types have no declared provider export and generation fails or requires their unassigned relocation.
witness.observer: The generator or developer assembling the modules.
basis:

topics.topic: Assignment, initial value, uniqueness, and advancement of session-local upload numbers
questions: Which module assigns the upload number, what is its initial value, and how is uniqueness within a session guaranteed across replacement uploads?
Which module assigns an upload's session-local number, what is its initial value, and how does it advance when an accepted upload replaces the prior file?

quotes:
`module:owner_sessions`. Keep an accepted upload in the session's memory,
replacing the session's earlier one (A16 rule 2).

The upload's number in the session: 1 for the session's first accepted
upload, then one more than the session's last, so two uploads of the same
bytes are two uploads (A16 rule 2).
judgement.why: State 5 assigns numbering to `owner_sessions`, starts it at 1, and advances it by one for every accepted replacement upload.

topics.topic: Authoritative ownership of A14 rules and the OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS mapping
questions: Does `audit_log` own all of A14, or do A14 rules 1 and 5 belong to `operations` as its section separately states?

How can `data_provider` own the action-to-audit-action mapping while its `Must not own` clause forbids it from owning behaviour or selection; is it authoritative policy, derived data, or merely storage for a decision owned elsewhere?
Is `data_provider` an A14 consumer or co-owner now that it owns and exports `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS`, and must the ownership table and `30_trace.json` include it?

quotes:
A14 and A15: appending an entry (M09) inside the transaction of the change it
records, with the next sequence number after the last the store's history ever
wrote, kept apart from the entries — M12 AuditSequence, made at 0 with a new
store — so an erasure never lowers it (A15 rule 5);

A14 rules 1 and 5:
appending the audit entry in the action's transaction when the action changed
state, its action the row of the data provider's `OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS` for
an owner action (owner, 2026-11-24).

The operation table: every operation of either surface with its stages and
the modules it changes — not which service may call it, which is the
release's table alone (A09 rule 2), asked of `service_access.service_may_call`
at stage (1); the owner's operations are the owner interface's.
judgement.why: P4 judged the same ownership boundary among `audit_log`, `operations`, and the data-provider routing and audit tables, and the quoted passages have not changed.

quotes:
the actions that write an entry and the subject each names (M09); the outcome
`accepted` (A14 rule 6); that no entry is ever changed (A15 rule 1); the
erasure before a date — not later than today, every entry before 00:00 UTC of
it removed, so that the erasure's own entry `operations` appends after it,
with its confirmation id, also when nothing was removed, is never removed by

Which action a request names, by its
method and path, and whether it is a change or touches an uploaded file, are
the rows of the data provider's `OWNER_ACTIONS`; its target is the query

precedent.why: The audit mapping, operation-table, and owner-routing passages are unchanged from the closed State 3, and the reopening changes did not make their division of responsibility newly material.

topics.topic: Division of responsibility for constructing and validating pending-confirmation bindings
questions: Which module owns constructing and comparing the import confirmation binding: `operations`, which owns this passage, or `owner_sessions`, which owns the pending confirmation and exposes `show_confirmation_step` and `take_confirmation`?

Does `operations` compare the submitted action, target, version and inputs with the pending binding, or does `owner_sessions.take_confirmation` perform that comparison and consume the value before returning an admission result?

quotes:
`module:owner_sessions`. Make the session's pending confirmation for an
action that asks for one (A13 rule 6).

The admitted session; the action; its target; the revision or access
version the step shows, or that it shows none; the action's inputs — for an
erasure its choice, for the import the upload's number and the file's
digest with the picks, names, aliases and Customer values, for an erasure
of old entries the date.

A session holds at most one pending confirmation (A13 rule 6); a
submission whose action, target, version or inputs differ from those shown
is not bound (A13 rule 6, test 12) — the inputs are kept as their digest,
this operation's way of binding them, never as values; the value never
appears in a URL, a log line, a diagnostic or an entry (A13 rule 7).

`module:owner_sessions`. Decide whether a submission carries the session's
pending confirmation, and use it up (A13 rule 6).
judgement.why: State 5 makes `operations` the caller that supplies the complete semantic inputs while `owner_sessions.show_confirmation_step` binds them and `owner_sessions.take_confirmation` compares and consumes the pending confirmation.

topics.topic: Authoritative computation and reuse of uploaded-file digests
questions: Which module computes the uploaded bytes' digest, which digest algorithm and byte representation are authoritative, and which modules receive rather than recompute it for M10, M14, M18, M21 and confirmation binding?

quotes:
The mapping names
the file by its digest. The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.
judgement.why: Although State 5 assigns digest computation to `migration_import` and delivery to `owner_sessions`, the digest algorithm and authoritative byte encoding are format and contract details owned by State 6, not module ownership in State 3.

quotes:
The session's pending confirmation is replaced: a new value from
`random_values.make_secret_value`, bound to the action, its target, what the
step showed and the digest of its inputs in a fixed order, and the reading
of `clock.monotonic_reading` it was shown at.

A session holds at most one pending confirmation (A13 rule 6); a
submission whose action, target, version or inputs differ from those shown
is not bound (A13 rule 6, test 12) — the inputs are kept as their digest,
this operation's way of binding them, never as values; the value never
appears in a URL, a log line, a diagnostic or an entry (A13 rule 7).

`module:owner_sessions`. Decide whether a submission carries the session's
pending confirmation, and use it up (A13 rule 6).
judgement.why: State 5 assigns the fixed-order input digest and its binding semantics to `owner_sessions.show_confirmation_step`, with `owner_sessions.take_confirmation` owning the corresponding comparison and consumption.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
